findings.evidence: grep `instance linearOrder : LinearOrder` hits in Mathlib/NumberTheory/Zsqrtd/Basic.lean:776, Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Order.lean:95; PR file line 138 `theorem exists_linearOrder`.
findings.issue: `RingPreordering.order` (and `OrderedSubfield.order` in OrderedSubfield.lean:75) are defs returning `LinearOrder`; rule 3 names functions after their return type, and the same file uses `exists_linearOrder`.

findings.evidence: Statements at the cited lines; `Odd p.natDegree` is the hypothesis, not 'odd order'.
findings.issue: `exists_odd_order` reads as a group-theoretic 'odd order'; the conclusion is `∃ o : LinearOrder (AdjoinRoot p)`. Same vocabulary in `exists_quadratic_order` (OrderExtension.lean:143), `exists_order_extension` (OrderExtension.lean:104), and the inconsistent pair `extensionCone.neg_one_notMem_of_odd` (line 63) vs `extensionCone.neg_one_notMem_quadratic` (OrderExtension.lean:129).
`base_strictMono : StrictMono (algebraMap K P.field)` and the field `base_nonneg` (line 33) use the ad-hoc word `base` where Mathlib names the map `algebraMap`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maximal.lean:80 `exists_le_maximal … ∃ M, M.IsMaximal ∧ I ≤ M`; Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Module/HahnEmbedding.lean:939 `theorem exists_isMax`; naming rule 5.
findings.issue: `exists_ordering : ∃ Q, P ≤ Q ∧ Q.IsOrdering` omits the `P ≤ Q` conclusion and spells the predicate `IsOrdering` as a noun. Likewise `OrderedSubfield.exists_maximal : ∃ P, IsMax P` (OrderedSubfield.lean:151) — Mathlib's `exists_maximal` lemmas are about `IsMaximal`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/UniqueFactorization.lean:72 `exists_irreducible_of_natDegree_pos : ∃ g, Irreducible g ∧ g ∣ f` is the name pattern for the weaker statement.
findings.issue: `exists_irreducible_factor_of_odd_natDegree` names only `∃ q, Irreducible q ∧ q ∣ p`; the actual content, `Odd q.natDegree`, is absent from the name, so it advertises the weaker statement Mathlib already has.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Ordering/Defs.lean:85-96 `toSubsemiring_*`; Cone.lean has no `cone` constructor precedent (only `nonneg : RingCone T`).
findings.issue: `RingPreordering.cone : RingCone K` is a structure conversion; rule 3 and Mathlib's own `RingPreordering.toSubsemiring` call these `toX`.

summary: Several names use ad-hoc or misleading vocabulary: `order` for defs returning `LinearOrder`, `odd_order`/`quadratic_order` for order-existence lemmas, `base_` for `algebraMap`, and `exists_ordering`/`exists_maximal` for `IsOrdering`/`IsMax` conclusions. Namespacing of the `RingPreordering` and `Polynomial` material is correct and no notation is introduced.
